❷#BUDDHISM
Budiizmiin amantii fi falaasama addunyaa guddaa yoo ta'u, waggoota 2,500 oliin dura Hinditti kan ka'e Siddhartha Gautama (Buddha, ykn "Isa Dammaqe") waliin, daandii gidiraa xumuruu (Dukkha) fi Nirvana (ibsa) galmaan ga'uuf shaakala akka xiinxala, amala naamusaa, fi ogummaatiin barsiisa, waaqa uumaa osoo hin taane guddina hafuuraa dhuunfaa irratti xiyyeeffachuun, fi itti amanuudhaan  karma fi reenkaarneeshinii.  Innis amantii waaqa hin qabne kan Dhugaawwan Kabajamoo Afur fi Daandii Saddeet irratti giddu galeessa godhate yoo ta'u, nagaa keessaa, sammuu fi waan hundumaa dhaabbataa ta'uu dhabuu cimsee kan ibsudha.

➨Amantii_fi_Yaad_rimee_Ijoo:
 ➨ Siddhartha Gautama (The Buddha): Barsiisaa hafuuraa kan ifa argate fi karaa namoota birootti agarsiise.
 ➨ Dharma: Barsiisa Buddha, hordoftoota qajeelchuu.
 ➨ Dhugaawwan Kabajamoo Afur: Jireenyi gidiraa of keessaa qaba (Dukkha);  gidiraan araada/itti maxxanuu irraa dhufa;  gidiraan xumuramuu danda’a;  karaan gidiraa fixu Daandii Saddeettamaa dha.
 ➨ Daandii Saddeet Kabajamaa: Qajeelfama qabatamaa jireenya naamusaa, naamusa sammuu fi ogummaa (hubannoo sirrii, yaada, dubbii, gocha, jireenya, carraaqqii, sammuu, xiyyeeffannaa).
 ➨ Karma: Seera sababaafi bu’aa;  gochoonni muuxannoo gara fuula duraa murteessu.
 Deebi’ee dhalachuu (Samsara): Marsaa dhalootaa, du’aa fi deebi’ee dhalachuu, kan Nirvaanaa ga’uudhaan mo’amu.
 ➨ Nirvaanaa: Galma dhumaa – haala bilisummaa, nagaa, fi fedhii fi gidiraa irraa bilisa ta’uu.
 Waaqummaa kan hin qabne: Waaqa uumaa tokkotti amanuu irratti kan xiyyeeffatu osoo hin taane, dhugoomsa dhuunfaa irratti kan xiyyeeffatudha.  

 ➨ Shaakala:
 ➨ Xiinxala: Xiyyeeffannoo fi hubannoo horachuu.
 ➨ Sammuu: Yeroo ammaa kanaaf xiyyeeffannoo kennuu.
 ➨ Safuu: Ajaja naamusaa hordofuu.
 ➨ Gara laafina & Ogummaa: Safuu keessaa guddisuu.  
➨ Ka’umsa fi Babal’ina:
 Hindii durii (Dh.K.D jaarraa 6ffaa-5ffaa) keessatti jalqabe.
 Guutummaa Eeshiyaa (Chaayinaa, Jaappaan, Kibba Baha Eeshiyaa) fi addunyaa irratti babal’ate.  
 Budiizmiin akka falaasama, akkaataa jireenyaa fi amantiitti kan ilaalamu yoo ta’u, daandii of guutuu fi hubannoo gadi fagoo jiraachuu dhiyeessa.

❸#HINDUISM
Hinduism maatii duudhaa hafuuraa Hindii adda addaa, amantiiwwan addunyaa durii keessaa tokko jedhamee kan ilaalamu, hundeessaa ykn barumsa jabaa tokko kan hin qabne, yaad-rimeewwan akka dharma (dirqama/naamusa), karma (gocha/bu’aa), samsara (marsaa deebi’ee dhalootaa), fi moksha (bilisummaa) irratti kan xiyyeeffate dha.  Hinduun waaqolii baay’ee kan waaqeffatu yoo ta’u, yeroo baay’ee akka mul’ata dhugaa isa dhumaa tokkicha, Biraaman, Viishnuu, Shiivaa fi Gaanesha dabalatee namoota gurguddoo wajjin kan ilaalamanidha.  Innis akkaataa jireenyaa barreeffamoota durii akka Veedaa keessatti hundee godhate yoo ta'u, jireenya qajeelaa fi dhugoomsa hafuuraa cimsee kan ibsudha.  
➨ Amantii fi Yaad-rimee Ijoo:
 ➨ Brahman: Dhugaa isa dhumaa, bifa hin qabne, kan waaqummaa, kan jiraachuun hundi irraa burqu fi itti deebi’u.
 ➨ Waaqolii: Waaqolii fi waaqoliin dubartootaa hedduun (akka Vishnu, Shiva, Devi, Ganesha) akka gama adda addaatti ykn mul’ata Brahmanitti kabajamu, waaqeffannaa adda addaa kan hayyamu.
 ➨ Dharma: Dirqama naamusaa fi naamusaa, amala qajeelaa fi sirna koosmii.
 ➨ Karma: Seera sababaafi bu’aa, kan gochoonni jireenya tokko keessatti raawwataman haala isa itti aanuu murteessan.
 ➨ Samsara: Marsaa walitti fufiinsa qabu kan dhalootaa, du’aa fi deebi’ee dhalachuu (deebi’ee dhalachuu).
 ➨ Moksha: Marsaa samsara irraa bilisa bahuu, tokkummaa hafuuraa waaqa wajjin galmaan gahuu.
 ➨ Ahimsaa: Jeequmsa malee, jireenya hunda akka qulqulluutti kabajuu. 
 Barreeffamoota Ijoo fi Ka’umsa:
 ➨ Ka’umsa: Waggoota 4,000 oliin dura ardii xiqqaa Hindii keessatti kan madde yoo ta’u, duudhaa Hindii durii irraa kan guddate yoo ta’u, hundeen isaa Qaroomina Gammoojjii Indus keessatti ta’uu danda’a.
 Caaffata Qulqullaa’oo: Barreeffamoonni qulqulluun ijoo Veedaa, Upanishad, Puranas, Mahabharata (Bhagavad Gita of keessaa qabu) fi Ramayana kan dabalatudha. 
 Garaagarummaa:
 Hinduism falaasama, gochaalee fi gareewwan adda addaa (akka Vaishnavism, Shaivism, Shaktism, Smartism) kan hammate yoo ta’u, ilaalcha waaqa mushrik, waaqa tokkoo, waaqa hundumaa, yookaan illee waaqa hin amanne dabalatee daandii adda addaa gara dhugaatti geessu ni hayyama.

❹#SHINTOISM
Shintoism amantii dhalootaan Jaappaan, "karaa waaqolii," hafuurota uumamaa (kami) meeshaalee uumamaa, abbootii fi gootota keessatti waaqeffachuu irratti kan xiyyeeffate yoo ta'u, qulqullina, walsimsiisaa fi sirna irratti cimsuudhaan dogmaa cimaa osoo hin taane, hundeessaa ykn kitaaba qulqulluu kan hin qabne, Budiizmii Jaappaan keessatti waliin jiraatu.  Sirna waaqa mushrik fi animistic kan kami waan hunda keessa jiraatu, karaa mana qulqullummaa (jinja), ayyaana, fi sirna kabajamu, namoota duudhaa isaanii durii fi addunyaa uumamaa waliin kan wal qunnamsiisudha. 
 ➨ Amantii fi Yaad-rimee Ijoo
 Kami: Hafuurota qulqulluu ykn waaqolii taateewwan uumamaa (bubbee, gaarreen, lageen) fi namoota adda ta’an keessa jiraatan;  Waaqni Aduu Amateraasu giddu galeessa dha.
➨ Qulqullina: Xiyyeeffannoo guddaa, faalama hafuuraa (kegare) balleessuuf sirna qulqulleessuu (dhiqachuu/dhiqachuu)tiin galma ga’a.
 ➨ Walsimsiisaa: Nama, uumama fi kamii gidduutti madaallii barbaaduu.
 ➨ Hidda dhalootaa: Miseensonni maatii du’an kami akaakayyuu ta’uu danda’u, karaa mana qulqullummaa maatii (kamidana) kabajama. 
 Shaakala & Sirna
➨ Manneen qulqullummaa (Jinja): Bakkeewwan waaqeffannaa kamii addaa, luboonni (kannushi) aarsaa fi sirna raawwatan.
➨ Ayyaanota (Matsuri): Ayyaana hawaasaa shubbisa (kagura) fi aarsaa kamiif dhiyeessuun.
# Sirna Dhiqachuu: Mana qulqulluutti dhiyaachuu ykn waaqeffannaa irratti bobba’uu dura barbaachisaa dha.
➨ Safuu Cimaa Hin Qabu: Duuti kami ta’uutti nama geessuu danda’us, seera naamusaa cimaa ykn barumsa jireenya boodaa irratti osoo hin taane, gochaa fi qulqullina jireenya kana keessatti irratti xiyyeeffata.  
 Hariiroo amantii Budiizimii wajjin qabu
 Shiintoon hafuura dhalootaa Jaappaan yoo ta'u, amantiin Budiizimii ammoo booda dhufe.
 Jaappaanonni hedduun waldhabdee malee lamaan isaaniiyyuu kan shaakalan yoo ta'u, taateewwan jireenyaaf (dhaloota, cidha) Shiintoo fi awwaalchaaf amantii Budiizimii fayyadamu.  
 Furtuu Fudhachuu
 Shintoon aadaa, duudhaa fi uumama Jaappaan wajjin gadi fageenyaan kan walqabate yoo ta’u, jireenya guyyaa guyyaa, hawaasaa fi kabaja qulqulluu addunyaa naannoo isaanii jiruuf akka bu’uura hafuuraatti tajaajila, akkuma Wiikiipiidiyaa irratti ibsame.  

❺#JUDAISM
Amantiin Yihudootaa amantii fi aadaa durii, waaqa tokkicha kan ummata Yihudootaa yoo ta’u, Abrahaam irraa jalqabee karaa Musee Siinaa irratti Toora (seera waaqayyoo) wajjin kan mul’ate Waaqayyo tokkicha isaan waliin kakuu galetti amanuu irratti kan xiyyeeffate dha.  Akkaataa jireenyaa hunda galeessa ta'eedha, abboommii Waaqayyoo hordofuu (mitzvot) karaa shaakala akka Shabbat, seera nyaataa (kosher), kadhannaa, fi qo'annootiin, haala hawaasaa cimaa keessatti cimsee kan ibsudha.
 Amantii fi Yaad-rimee Ijoo
➨ Waaqa Tokkicha: Uumaa tokkicha, kan hin qoodamne, humna hundumaa danda’u tokkotti amanuu.
➨ Kakuu (Brit): Waaqayyo saba Yihudootaa wajjin waliigaltee addaa, saba ta’uu fi qajeelfama isaaniif waadaa gale.
➨ Tooraa fi Taalmuud: Tooraan (kitaabonni Macaafa Qulqulluu shanan jalqabaa) seera Waaqayyoo kan of keessaa qabu yoo ta’u, Taalmuud marii fi hiika raabii bal’aa kan walitti qabame yoo ta’u, bu’uura seeraa fi duudhaa Yihudootaa kan uumudha.
➨ Mitzvot (Abboommii): Abboommii waaqummaa 613 kan jireenya Yihudootaa qajeelchan, naamusa, sirna fi amala guyyaa guyyaa kan uwwisu.
➨ Masiihii: Hiikni garaa garaa ta’us, Masiihii gara fuulduraatti bara nagaa fi haqaa addunyaa maraa fidutti amanuu. 
 Muuxannoowwan Ijoo & Kabajamoo
➨ Shabbat (Sanbata): Torbanitti guyyaa boqonnaa fi haaromsa hafuuraa Jimaata galgalaa hanga Dilbata galgalaatti.
➨ Kadhannaa: Kadhannaa guyyaa guyyaa, Sheemaa (labsii tokkummaa Waaqayyoo) dabalatee.
➨ Ayyaana: Ayyaanota akka Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Faasikaa fi Hanukkah kabajuu.
 Seerota Nyaataa (Kosher): Seerota nyaata hayyamamuu fi qophii ilaalchisee.
➨ Mana sagadaa: Mana waaqeffannaa fi giddugala hawaasaa.  
 Eenyummaa & Hawaasa
➨ Ethnic & Religious: Yihudummaan amantii fi eenyummaa sabaa ummata Yihudootaa yoo ta’u, hidhata aadaa cimaa qaba.
➨ Dameewwan: Waldoonni gurguddoon Ortodoksii (ciminaan hordofuu), Konsarvaatiivii (hiikkaa ammayyaa), fi Haaromsa (liberal adaptation) kan dabalatudha.  
 Hariiroo Amantii Biroo Waliin Qabu
➨ Amantii Abrahaam: "Amantii haadha" kan Kiristaanummaa fi Islaamummaan irraa guddate jedhamee fudhatama, hundi isaanii Abrahaam irraa kan dhufanidha.

❻#TAOISM
Taoism (ykn Daoism) falaasamaa fi amantii dhalootaan Chaayinaa Tao (ykn Dao) wajjin walsimsiisuun jiraachuu giddu galeessa godhate, bu'uuraa, kan hin dubbatamne "Kara" ykn "Daandii" uumama cufaa, uumamaa, salphaa, fi gocha dadhabbii malee (wu wei) cimsee.  Innis falaasama (Dàojiā) fi amantii (Dàojiào) shaakala akka xiinxala, tai chi, fi alchemy kan qabu, of guddisuu fi hafuuraan hin duune irratti kan xiyyeeffate, barreeffamoota akka Tao Te Ching tiin kan qajeelfamuudha.  
 Yaad-rimee fi Amantii Ijoo
 Tao (Dao): Qajeelfama dhumaa, maqaa hin qabnee fi madda waan hundumaa, dhangala’aa uumamaa uumama cufaa bakka bu’a.
➨ Yin fi Yang: Yaad-rimee humnoota dabalataa, walfaallaa (akka dukkanaa/ifa, dabarsoo/sochii) kanneen madaallii fi jijjiirama uumama cufa keessatti uumuu.
➨ Wu Wei: "Gocha carraaqqii malee" ykn "gochuu dhiisuu," humnaan carraaquu caalaa, uumamaan, ofumaan Tao wajjin walsimsiisuun socho'uu.
 Qabeenya Sadan: Gara laafina, qusannaa fi gad of qabuu.  
 Shaakala & Galmoota
➨ Qonna Hafuuraa: Shaakala akka xiinxala, shaakala hafuura baafachuu (Qigong), fi alkeemii keessoo walsimsiisaa keessaa fi umurii dheeraa argachuuf kan kaayyeffate dha.
 Uumama wajjin walsimsiisuun: Galmi ijoo ta’e, sirbaafi akkaataa addunyaa uumamaa wajjin walsimsiisuun jiraachuudha.
➨ Of Fooyyessu: Ofittummaa hir’isuu, fedhii salphisuu fi dhugummaa uumamaa (ziran) hammachuu irratti xiyyeeffata.  
 Barreeffamoota Ijoo & Ka'umsa
➨ Tao Te Ching (Daodejing): Naannoo jaarraa 6ffaa Dh.K.D.tti Laozi (Lao Tzu) jedhamuun kan waamamu yoo ta’u, barreeffamni bu’uuraa kun maalummaa Tao qorata.
➨ Ka'umsa: Amantii ummata Chaayinaa durii irraa kan guddate yoo ta'u, falaasamaafi amantiitti kan ilaalamu yoo ta'u, yeroo baayyee aadaa Chaayinaa keessatti Konfishiyaanismii fi Budiizimii waliin kan walqabatudha.

❼#JAINISM
Jainism amantii Hindii durii qulqullina hafuuraa, ifa ta’uu fi bilisummaa (moksha) irratti kan xiyyeeffate karaa jeequmsa hin qabne (ahimsa) lubbu qabeeyyii hunda irratti, of adabuu fi walitti hidhamiinsa dhabuudhaan.  Jainoonni barsiisota geggeessitoota hafuuraa 24 Tirthankaras jedhaman irraa argatan hordofu, Mahaviraan isa dhiyoo fi beekamaa ta'ee, akkasumas foon uffachuutti amanu, bakka karma gocha irraa (keessumaa namoota biroo miidhuu) deebi'ee dhalachuu murteessa.  Qajeeltoowwan ijoo ahimsa (jekkora hin qabne), anekāntavāda (absolutism/dhugaa gama hedduu qabu), fi aparigraha (qabachuu dhabuu) of keessatti qabatu. 
 Amantii fi Hojii Ijoo
➨ Ahimsa (Jeequmsa malee): Yaadannoo giddugaleessaa, bifa lubbu qabeeyyii hunda (nama, bineensota, biqiltoota, maaykiroobii illee) kan babal’atu, gara vegetarianism cimaatti kan geessu, kuduraalee hundee irraa fagaachuu, fi of eeggannoo garmalee ilbiisota akka hin miidhaneef.
➨ Karma & Reincarnation: Gochoonni karma uumu, marsaa dhalootaa, du’aa fi deebi’anii dhalachuu (samsara) irratti dhiibbaa geessisu.
 Moksha (Bilisummaa): Galmi dhumaa fedhii mo’achuu fi waan hunda beekuu galmaan ga’uudhaan marsaa kana irraa bilisa ba’uudha.
➨ Tirthankaras: Barsiisota hafuuraa (akka Mahavira) kanneen namoota biroo gara ifaatti qajeelchan;  Jain akka fakkeenyaatti malee akka waaqatti isaan kabaju.
 Anekāntavāda (Non-absolutism): Yaada dhugaan gama hedduu qaba, gad of qabuu fi wal danda’uu sammuu guddisa.
➨ Asceticism: Of to’achuu, xiinxaluu fi qabeenya addunyaa irraa adda bahuu cimsa, keessumaa monoksootaa fi abbootii amantiitiif. 
 Amaloota Ijoo
 Ka'umsa Durii: Duudhaa Hindii durii keessaa tokko, amantii Budiizimii dura ture.
➨ Waaqa Uumaa Hin Qabu: Yuunivarsiitiin ofumaan kan to’atu, uumaa olaanaa kan hin qabne ta’uu isaa ni amana.
➨ Bu’uura Naamusaa: Naamusa naamusaa irratti kan xiyyeeffatu yoo ta’u, dubbisuu fi barreessuu olaanaa fi daldala keessatti gahee amanamaa akka qabaatu taasisa. 
➨ Fakkeenya Shaakala: Nyaata
 Jains vegetarian ciccimoo fi yeroo baayyee vegan yoo ta'an, kuduraalee hundee (akka boqqolloo, basaqaa, garlic) irraa fagaatu sababiin isaas isaan sassaabuun biqiltuu guutuu ajjeesa, tokko tokko immoo nyaata damma qabu (akka alkoolii) irraa fagaatu sababiin isaas daakuun bifa jireenyaa daqiiqaa balleessuu waan of keessaa qabuuf.

❽#ATHEISM
Waaqayyoon hin amanne amantii osoo hin taane waaqolii ykn waaqoliitti amanuu dhabuudha, bu’uuraan waan uumamaa ol ta’etti amanuun dhabuu, yeroo baay’ee safuudhaaf sababa, saayinsii fi naamusa addunyaa irratti hirkatanii jiraachuu, haa ta’u malee warri Waaqayyoon hin amanne ilaalcha adda addaa fi bu’uura naamusaa qabaatanis, akkuma namoota dhuunfaa amantii. Many families breakdowns today, a reflection of; not a moral failure, but governance failure within the household, the customary system resonating the Karl Max’s theory of control.

Date: 12 January 2025

Recently, during an informal discussion at our usual table of like minds, a colleague posed an intriguing question, “Daniel! How do you address the question of power control at your table?”
At first glance, this question was not straightforward, and I chose not to respond immediately. Instead, I decided to reflect on it holistically and share my thoughts in a structured manner. My intention is not only to address the concern raised but also to provide insights for others who may be grappling with similar questions, particularly on the issue of power control within family settings.
To approach this, I will draw on two perspectives, a) the Concept of Power through Karl Marx’s Theory of Control.  In this concept, Marx’s theory emphasizes the dynamics of power as a tool for control, often linked to resources and authority. Applying this lens, power at any table, be it organizational or familial, can be understood as the ability to influence decisions, allocate resources, and shape outcomes. The challenge lies in ensuring that such power is exercised equitably and responsibly, avoiding domination or marginalization.
b) a Customary Perspective, beyond theoretical frameworks, power control is deeply rooted in cultural norms and traditions. In many societies, family structures and community interactions dictate how authority is shared or concentrated. Addressing power control at the family level requires balancing respect for tradition with principles of fairness and mutual understanding.
Ultimately, power should not be viewed as a weapon but as a shared responsibility, a means to foster harmony, accountability, and collective progress.
In South Sudan, the family is not merely a private arrangement between two individuals; it is a social institution, historically regulated by customary law, kinship systems, and communal expectations. Long before modern constitutions or development models, societies such as the Dinka and Nuer understood that family stability depends on clear authority, structured control of resources, and collective purpose.
When examined carefully, these customary systems resonate strongly with Karl Marx’s theory of control, which argues that stability in any system, whether a state, an economy, or a household, depends on how resources are controlled, how authority is structured, and whether power is coordinated rather than fragmented.

Marx viewed society through the lens of material relations, who controls resources, who makes decisions, and how power is exercised. In African societies, and particularly among the Dinka and Nuer, the household has always been treated as a unit of production and not as a collection of competing individuals.
Marriage under customary law is a contract between lineages, secured through bridewealth (cattle). Children belong to the husband’s clan, property is held for the lineage, and household decisions carry social consequences beyond the couple. This structure reflects a fundamental principle, resources must be managed in an organized and centralized manner to preserve unity.
Among the Dinka and Nuer, cattle are the primary means of production, social security, and cultural capital. Customary law is explicit on this point, cattle are owned by the lineage, not by individual spouses. The husband manages cattle as a custodian, not an absolute owner. Disposal of major assets requires consultation with elders and kin. Women exercise authority over internal household economy, milk, food, children, and social relations, but not ultimate ownership of lineage property.
This arrangement is not accidental. It prevents the emergence of competing centers of power within the household. In Marxist terms, customary law deliberately avoids an internal “class struggle” by ensuring that control over the means of production is coordinated, regulated, and socially accountable.
Modern discourse increasingly promotes full financial autonomy within marriage, often without regard to African social structures. While autonomy and dignity are important, applying this concept without structural adaptation can destabilize families.
When both spouses exercise independent and equal control over household resources without a clear governance framework, the family risks, rival decision-making, conflicting priorities, erosion of respect, persistent disputes over authority.
Marx would describe this as a structural contradiction, two powers attempting to control the same productive unit without coordination. Customary law anticipated this risk and therefore placed financial leadership within a defined authority, balanced by consultation and communal oversight.
It is essential to clarify that customary authority is not synonymous with oppression. In Dinka and Nuer societies, household leadership is constrained by, moral obligations, kinship accountability, Intervention by elders, sanctions for abuse of authority
Women’s natal families retain influence, and persistent mistreatment can trigger clan-level consequences. Authority is therefore socially regulated, not absolute. This aligns with Marxist theory, which holds that control is legitimate only when it serves the collective interest of the system.
Antonio Gramsci’s concept of consent helps explain why customary systems endured. Authority in traditional households was accepted because it was culturally legitimate and socially embedded. Decisions were guided by precedent, elders mediated disputes, and the family’s ideology emphasized unity over individual power. Control was maintained not through coercion, but through shared belief in the system’s purpose.
Importantly, these customary principles are not legally obsolete. South Sudan’s Transitional Constitution recognizes customary law and traditional authority as sources of law, and courts are required to apply customary norms where they are not inconsistent with the constitution or statutory law.
This constitutional framework affirms that customary rules governing marriage, property, and family relations, such as those practiced by the Dinka and Nuer, remain legally relevant. As such, arguments for structured household authority are not merely cultural preferences; they are grounded in recognized legal tradition. 
Urbanization, wage labor, and externally driven empowerment models have transformed household economics. However, when individual financial autonomy is introduced without redefining household authority, families often experience confusion and conflict.
From a Marxist perspective, this outcome is predictable: new economic relations imposed on old social systems without structural adjustment produce instability. Many family breakdowns today reflect not moral failure, but governance failure within the household.
Finally structure as the Foundation of Stability the Dinka and Nuer customary law, reinforced by Marxist theory, teaches a simple but powerful lesson: families thrive on structured authority, coordinated resource control, and shared purpose.
Equality without structure invites rivalry. Authority without accountability invites abuse. Stability lies in a system where leadership is clear, control is regulated, and consent is culturally grounded. There is no middle way.

Daniel

Their quest to reclaim it mirrors the broader struggle to liberate Chittagong and British India. Abhishek Bachchan delivers a nuanced portrayal, complemented by the restrained authenticity of Deepika Padukone and Sikandar Kher. Why Nuerland shouldn’t be a war Zone

The politic in South Sudan have divided siblings into IG or IO. The problem of South Sudan politics is that we point guns against each opposing parties to pass our message. Yes it’s true politic can be a “ dirty game” but do we have to created our own blood bath to prove a point, absolutely not. My sincere advise to Nuer forces IG and IO don’t kill each other based on political differences, any Nuer life taken in battle is a loss for both sides. 
Nuer SPLM IG in Nuer land should give a peaceful passage for IO to Juba and meet Kiir forces plus UPDF. Don’t give Kiir the impression that Nuer land is a circus 🤡, don’t be a laughingstock. A win for IO is a win for all of us.
Recently in Guit county of Bentiu, where brother fought brother, blood by blood, because of political differences.what do we gain, nothing but a batch of fools. The same notion is happening across all Nuerland. That why I said Nuerland shouldn’t be a war zone for Kiir and his Dinka elite to stay in power. Whoever needs to challenge or support Kiir both need to do so freely in Juba. Go do your fight away from us.

Be like Lou Nuer

Lou Nuer even though they were being infiltrated by few elements of brotherly politics, they have still emerged victorious without causing unnecessary bloodshed. They truly understand the consequences of political violence especially when blood relatives lives are at stake. Lou Nuer are one of the largest Nuer sector in the land, if they can unite why not us. Our hopes are with Lou Nuer community, maybe your unity will be imitated by other Nuer communities.

ANG KWENTO NI HUDAIFAH IBN AL YAMAN RA.

ANG TAGA PAG INGAT NG LIHIM NG SUGO NG ALLAH SW.

Si Hudhayfah Ibn al-Yaman ay isa sa mga naunang nagbalik-loob sa Islam at nagbahagi ng napakalapit na kaugnayan sa Sugo ng Allah Sumakanya nawa ang kapayapaan at pagpapala ng Allah.  

Ang kanyang ama na si al-Yaman ay mula sa Makkah, ngunit kinailangang tumakas sa Medina dahil siya ay nakapatay ng isang tao sa Makkah.  

Bagama't ang pagbabawal sa kanya na pumasok sa Makkah ay inalis pagkaraan ng ilang panahon, pinili niyang gawin ang Medina bilang kanyang tirahan at samakatuwid si Hudhayfah, sa kabila ng pagiging isang Makkan, ay pinalaki siya sa Medina.

Ang malapit na kaugnayan na ibinahagi niya sa Sugo ng Allah ay nagbigay-daan sa kanya na magsalaysay ng malaking bilang ng mga ahadith, partikular na nauugnay sa katapusan ng mga panahon, ang eschatology.  

Ang pagiging isang Makkan na pinalaki sa Medina ay lumikha ng isang maliit na krisis sa pagkakakilanlan para kay Hudhayfah at kaya nang makilala niya ang Sugo ng Allah ay tinanong niya siya kung siya ay isang muhajir o ansar.  

Ang Sugo ay sumagot, "Kung nais mo ay maaari mong ituring ang iyong sarili na kabilang sa mga muhajirin, o kung nais mo ay maaari mong ituring ang iyong sarili na isa sa mga Ansar.  Piliin mo kung alin ang mas mahal mo.

Kalaunan ay pinili ni Hudhayfah na manatiling ansar.

Ang pagsasama ni Hudhayfah sa Sugo ng Allah ay lumago pangunahin sa Medina at ang una ay magiting na lumahok sa lahat ng mga labanan at mga ekspedisyong militar maliban sa Labanan sa Badr.  

Ang kanyang pagmamahal sa Islam at ang kanyang walang patid na pananampalataya kay Allah ay maiisip mula sa kasawiang nangyari sa Labanan sa Uhud.  

Ang kanyang ama, si al-Yaman, ay nakikipaglaban sa mga Mushrik nang kinuha siya ng isa sa mga Muslim bilang isang Mushrik at inatake siya, na kalaunan ay humantong sa kanyang kamatayan.

Si Hudhayfah ay nagpakita ng tapang at lakas at sinabi sa mga pumatay sa kanyang ama, Nawa'y patawarin kayo ng Diyos dahil Siya ang Pinakamaawain sa mga nagpapakita ng awa.

Ang kanyang pagmamahal sa Islam ay higit pa sa pagmamahal sa kanyang ama at sa paghihiganti sa kanyang mga pumatay at tinanggihan pa niya ang perang kabayaran (diyah) at sinabi, Siya ang kanyang ama ay naghahanap lamang ng shahadah at nakamit niya ito.  

Diyos ko!  Magpatotoo na ibinibigay ko ang kabayaran para sa kanya sa mga Muslim.

 Dahil sa pagkakaroon ng mga Hudyo at ilang mapagkunwari na mga Muslim, ang Medina ay naging sentro ng mga sabwatan.  

Ang mga pagsasabwatan ay ginawa laban sa Islam at laban sa Sugo ng Allah kung kaya't noon pa nila binalak na patayin ang Sugo.  

Ang mga mapagkunwari ay sinubukang magsagawa ng isang ganoong plano isang araw at sinubukang patayin ang Sugo ng Allah, gayunpaman iniligtas siya ng Allah at ang mga umaatake ay tumakas.  

Walang makakita kung sino sila habang itinago nila ang kanilang mga mukha sa likod ng belo.  

Gayunpaman, alam ng Sugo ng Allah sumakanya nawa ang kapayapaan at mga pagpapala ng Allah kung sino sila at sinabi kay Hudhaifah ang mga pangalan ng mga mapagkunwari at binalaan siya na huwag ibuhos ang mga butil.  

lihim na sinabi sa kanya ng Sugo at mula noon ay nakuha ang titulong "Ang Tagapag-ingat ng Lihim ng Sugo ng Allah.

Kilala siya sa kanyang likas na may takot sa Diyos at kabanalan.  

Palagi niyang pinapayuhan ang mga kasama tungkol sa kahalagahan ng pag-uutos ng mabuti at pagbabawal ng masama at babalaan sila sa mga kahihinatnan nito, kung hindi nila ito gagawin.  

Sinabi ni Abu Ar-Riqad, Narinig ko si Hudhaifah na nagsabi, Ang isang tao ay nagbibigkas ng isang salita noong panahon ng Sugo ng Allah at naging mapagkunwari dahil dito.  

Apat na beses kong naririnig ang mga ganyang salita mula sa isa sa iisang upuan.  

Katiyakan, kayo ay mag-uutos ng mabuti, magbawal sa kasamaan at maghihikayat sa isa't isa na gumawa ng mabuti o palibutan kayong lahat ng Allah ng pagdurusa, o gagawin ninyong mga pinuno ang masasama sa inyo.  

Ang matuwid sa inyo ay magsusumamo, ngunit ang kanilang pagsusumamo ay hindi tatanggapin.

Ang kanyang pananalita ay parang isang pilosopo kaysa isang ordinaryong taong may kaalaman.  

Nagsasalita siya noon sa mga paraan na kikiliti sa katalinuhan ng nakikinig at makakaakit sa nakikinig sa kanya.  

Dati niyang sinasabi na mag-ingat sa Khushoo pagpakumbaba at debosyon sa pagdarasal sa pagpapaimbabaw.  

Nang tanungin siya kung ano itong Khushoo sa pagkukunwari, sinabi niya, Kapag ang katawan ay nagpapakita ng Khushoo, ngunit walang Khushoo sa puso.

Inuri pa niya ang puso sa apat na kategorya.  Minsan niyang sinabi, May apat na uri ng puso.  Ang puso na nakabalot o atrophied.  

Iyan ang puso ng kafir o walang utang na loob na hindi naniniwala.  Ang puso na hinubog sa manipis na patong.  

Iyan ang puso ng munafiq o mapagkunwari.  Ang pusong bukas at hubad at kung saan kumikinang ang isang maningning na liwanag.  Iyan ang puso ng mumin o mananampalataya.  

Sa wakas ay mayroong puso kung saan mayroong parehong pagkukunwari at pananampalataya.  

Ang pananampalataya ay tulad ng isang puno na namumulaklak sa mabuting tubig at ang pagkukunwari ay tulad ng isang abscess na umuunlad sa nana at dugo.  

Alinman ang higit na umunlad, maging ang puno ng pananampalataya o ang abscess ng pagkukunwari, ang siyang mananalo sa puso.

Dahil si Hudhaifah ay nasiyahan sa pakikisama at pagtitiwala ng Sugo ng Allah, siya ang pinagkatiwalaan ng Sugo upang makalusot sa kampo ng mga Mushrikeen sa panahon ng Labanan sa Trench.  

Ang Labanan sa Trench ay maaaring maging isang napakaseryosong labanan dahil ang mga Muslim ay humigit-kumulang na nasa pagitan ng mga Mushrik sa unahan at mga Hudyo mula sa Banu Quaraiza sa likuran.  

Sa ganitong maigting na sitwasyon na ipinadala ng Sugo ng Allah si Hudhaifah upang kumuha ng impormasyon tungkol sa bloke ng kaaway.  

Bago siya ipadala, ang Sugo ay nanalangin at nagsabi, O Panginoon, protektahan mo siya mula sa harap at mula sa likuran, mula sa kanyang kanan at mula sa kanyang kaliwa, mula sa itaas at mula sa ibaba.  

Sa sandaling natapos ng Sugo ang pagdarasal, si Hudhaifah ay nakadama ng lubos na kalmado at walang takot at pumasok sa kampo at bumalik na may dalang impormasyon na ligtas at maayos.

Sa panahon ng caliphate ni Umar (nawa'y kalugdan siya ng Allah), si Hudhaifah ay ginawang gobernador ng Kufah at Ctesiphon.  Gayunpaman, ang kanyang dalisay na pagiging simple, mapagpakumbaba at mapagpakumbaba na kalikasan ay nahuli sa mga tao ng Ctesiphon sa lubos na pagkabigla.  

Dahil sanay na ang mga tao sa karangyaan at kadakilaan ng mga naunang tagapamahala ng Persia, hindi nila maintindihan ang isang gobernador, nakasakay sa isang asno at kumakain ng isang tinapay.  

Pagdating niya, kinausap niya ang mga tao at sinabi, Mag-ingat sa mga lugar ng fitnah.  Nagtanong ang mga tao, Ano ang mga lugar ng fitnah.  

Sumagot si Hudhaifah, Ang mga pintuan ng mga pinuno kung saan pinupuntahan ng ilang tao at sinisikap na papaniwalain ang pinuno o gobernador ng kasinungalingan at pinupuri siya para sa mga katangiang hindi niya taglay.

SKANDAL IM PALAST: Die dunkle Wahrheit hinter der Bilderbuch-Ehe von Prinzessin Victoria – Was die Royals jahrelang verschwiegen!

Jeder erinnert sich an diese Bilder: Die Kathedrale von Stockholm, das Läuten der Glocken, prachtvolle Uniformen, fließende Kleider und die Gesichter eines ganzen Volkes, die auf eine einzige Frau gerichtet waren. Eine Prinzessin, die zum Altar schreitet, als wüsste sie bereits, dass dieser Tag tief in das Gedächtnis eines ganzen Landes eingebrannt bleiben würde. Doch wer sich nur an die ästhetische Schönheit der Zeremonie erinnert, verpasst den entscheidenden Teil der Geschichte. Denn die Wahrheit über die Ehe von Prinzessin Victoria von Schweden ist keine einfache Erzählung über glitzernde Diademe. Es ist eine Geschichte des Überlebens, eine Geschichte harter Entscheidungen und ein jahrelanger Kampf, in dem das vermeintliche Märchen einem gnadenlosen Test glich. Es war, als müsste die Liebe eine staatliche Prüfung ablegen, und die alles entscheidende Frage war brutal: Wie konnte eine Thronfolgerin, die von Kindheit an in ein Korsett aus Pflichten gezwängt und unter permanenter Beobachtung aufgezogen wurde, eine Liebe aufbauen, die stark genug war, um gegen den Druck der Tradition, schwere Krankheiten, bösartige Gerüchte und den unerbittlichen Blick der Weltöffentlichkeit zu bestehen?

Was Sie hier lesen werden, ist keine bloße Aufzählung von Daten. Es ist der Blick hinter die Kulissen, in die verschlossenen Zimmer, in das Schweigen der viel zu langen Nächte und die Ängste, die hinter einem makellosen Lächeln verborgen bleiben. Victoria wurde 1977 geboren und war vom Moment ihrer ersten Atemzüge an eine Person des öffentlichen Interesses. Als Erstgeborene des Königs und der Königin schien ihre Rolle klar, doch der Schein trügte. Zum Zeitpunkt ihrer Geburt garantierten die Gesetze noch nicht, dass das erstgeborene Kind den Thron erben würde. Erst als Schweden seine Verfassung änderte, wurde das kleine Mädchen plötzlich zur Zukunft der gesamten Monarchie. Stellen Sie sich vor, was das mit einem Kind macht: Bevor man überhaupt begreift, was ein Thron ist, wird man bereits als nationales Projekt, als Hoffnungsträger und Symbolfigur betrachtet. Das ganze Land beobachtet dich wie eine Uhr – man muss funktionieren, man muss durchhalten, man muss perfekt sein.

The Assam Tribune 

What makes a good war film? Brazen, gratuitous violence? Reckless, brave protagonists? Jingoistic nationalism? Or one that balances national pride with a nuanced human portrayal of a conflict’s universal tragedy and cost. Well, the choice is yours. For me, on any given day, a good war film is a film that’s anti-war. And Ikkis is one such honest, grounded, gritty gem that might (hopefully) change the discourse around Indian war films for good.

A Sriram Raghavan film is rarely a disappointment, but for a director who thrives on thrillers, it was a bold entry into unchartered territory, one that he has aced. Raghavan has not only drawn on the real-life story of a young soldier who dies on the battlefield but he has enriched the narrative by juxtaposing it with the story of an ageing father who journeys into that same battlefield, trying to comprehend his dead son’s final moments.

Second Lieutenant Arun Khetarpal is that Ikkis-year-old tank commander who makes the supreme sacrifice on December 16, 1971 during the Battle of Basantar. Thirty years later, his father, Brigadier M.L. Khetarpal, visits Lahore, to attend a college reunion, only to be hosted by the Pakistani soldier who had faced Arun in that battle.

A perfect plot that needed a perfect cast and Ikkis managed to orchestrate that as well.

Dharmendra as the affable old Brigadier was a revelation; a better swansong couldn’t have been written for a legend like him. Agastya Nanda has grown leaps and bounds since his Archies days and he will surely remind you of a young Abhishek Bacchhan from Refugee. As for Jaideep Ahlawat, it’s another masterclass on understated brilliance. It seems the man can do no wrong.

As Bollywood gleefully panders to jingoism in the name of nationalism, here comes a film that deftly handles a sensitive story without any agenda-driven narrative, without any Pakistan-bashing sequence, without equating ultranationalism with patriotism, simply offering a humane take on the cost of war, whichever side of the border you live in.

Es gibt Arten von Stille, die sich nicht wie Ruhe anfühlen. Es gibt eine Stille, die klingt wie eine Tür, die lautlos ins Schloss fällt, wie ein Licht, das ohne Vorwarnung erlischt, oder wie eine Hand, die sich gerade weit genug zurückzieht, damit es jeder bemerkt. Monatelang war die Welt von einem einzigen Detail besessen: Serena Williams ist nicht mehr so oft an der Seite von Alexis Ohanian zu sehen. Die gemeinsamen Fotos wurden seltener, die öffentlichen Gesten diskreter. In einer Welt, in der wir glauben, die Wahrheit zu kennen, nur weil wir drei Bilder und eine Story gesehen haben, füllte diese Leere ganze Romane. Sie lassen sich scheiden – so hallte es erst als Murmeln, dann als Gewissheit und schließlich als Urteil durch das Netz.

Doch hier beginnt das eigentliche Problem. Wenn sich ein Beziehungsgerücht an eine Frau wie Serena Williams heftet, ist das kein simpler Klatsch. Es ist eine Lupe, eine Treibjagd, eine Menschenmenge, die sich berechtigt fühlt, in ein Haus einzudringen, in das sie nie eingeladen wurde. Aber die wichtigste Frage ist nicht: Lassen sie sich scheiden? Die Frage, die einem wirklich die Kehle zuschnürt, ist: Wie fühlt es sich an, Serena zu sein, wenn die Welt entscheidet, dass dein Privatleben zum Spektakel werden muss? Es liegt eine fast grausame Absicht darin, eine Legende fallen sehen zu wollen – als ob man den Gedanken nicht ertragen könnte, dass eine Frau auf dem Platz unbesiegbar und in ihrer Familie stabil sein kann.

South Sudan’s Cry for Unity: 
When a Young Nation Bleeds, Africa Must Listen

South Sudan was born with immense hope, carrying the dreams of a people who had endured decades of struggle for self-determination. Yet years after independence, that promise remains painfully unfulfilled. Instead of peace, many citizens have known fear; instead of unity, deep divisions have been widened by a system of power built on tribal lines. 

Under the leadership of President Salva Kiir and his allies, governance has too often resembled a closed prison, one where ordinary people pay the price for political survival games. The result has been prolonged suffering, displacement, and a generation of youth growing up amid violence rather than opportunity.

The pain of South Sudan is not the pain of one tribe alone. While the Nuer community has suffered greatly, so too have the Dinka and the rest of the nation’s 63 tribes. This is not a tribal war of the people; it is a crisis of injustice, exclusion, and leadership that benefits from division. 

Many South Sudanese youths are not calling for revenge or hatred, they are calling for liberation from fear, for dignity, and for a country where identity is not used as a weapon. They yearn for a South Sudan where citizenship matters more than ethnicity, and where power serves the people rather than silences them.

Africa cannot afford to look away. Silence only deepens wounds and normalizes suffering. South Sudan’s story is a reminder that true independence is not just raising a flag, but building justice, unity, and accountable leadership. As an African proverb says, “When elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers.” In South Sudan, it is the ordinary people, the youth, women, and children who remain the grass under the weight of political battles. Their cry is simple but powerful: unity over division, truth over fear, and a future where all South Sudanese can stand as one nation.

A drum beaten for division will eventually call enemies to the village.

Birth name: Ilyena Vasilievna Mironoff
Story: Mirren's paternal grandfather was a
Russian diplomat who was negotiating an arms
deal in Great Britain when he and his family were
abruptly left stranded there with the outbreak of
the Russian Revolution. He became a cab driver
in London to support his family, and the Mironoff's
never left. In the 1950s, when the actress was
only 10, her father, Vasily Petrovich Mironoff,
legally changed his name to Basil Mirren and
decided to anglicize the rest of his family's names
so they'd fit in. Thus, Ilyena became Helen.

Dame Helen Mirren (80) wurde erst vor wenigen Tagen, am 8. Januar 2026, mit dem prestigeträchtigen Cecil B. DeMille Award für ihr Lebenswerk geehrt. Die Zeremonie fand im Rahmen des neuen Specials „Golden Eve“ vor den eigentlichen Golden Globes statt, wo sie von Weggefährten wie Harrison Ford als „Badass“ gewürdigt wurde. 
Aktuelle & kommende Projekte
Die Oscar-Preisträgerin bleibt eine der meistbeschäftigten Ikonen Hollywoods:
Switzerland: Aktuell verkörpert sie die Krimiautorin Patricia Highsmith in dem Psychothriller unter der Regie von Anton Corbijn.
The Thursday Murder Club: In der Verfilmung des Bestsellers von Richard Osman spielt sie die ehemalige Spionin Elizabeth Best (veröffentlicht 2025 auf Netflix).
Goodbye June: Zuletzt war sie im Familiendrama von und mit Kate Winslet zu sehen, das Ende 2025 Premiere feierte.
1923: Mirren setzt ihre Rolle als Cara Dutton in der Paramount+ Western-Serie fort. 
Meilensteine ihrer Karriere
Mirren ist eine der wenigen Schauspielerinnen, die die „Triple Crown of Acting“ (Oscar, Emmy, Tony) erreicht haben: 
Oscar: Beste Hauptdarstellerin für The Queen (2006).
Kultrollen: Bekannt aus Prime Suspect, Gosford Park und dem Fast & Furious-Franchise.

Harrison Ford (geboren am 13. Juli 1942 in Chicago, Illinois) ist ein amerikanischer Schauspieler, der für seine ikonischen Rollen als Han Solo in der Star Wars-Saga und als Titelfigur in der Indiana Jones-Reihe bekannt ist. Trotz seines Alters hat er keine Pläne, sich zur Ruhe zu setzen, und ist weiterhin aktiv in Film- und Fernsehproduktionen. 
Aktuelle Projekte und Auftritte
Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU): Ford übernahm die Rolle des President Thaddeus Ross (später als Red Hulk) im Film Captain America: Brave New World, der im Februar 2025 veröffentlicht wurde. Er wird die Rolle in einem weiteren kommenden Marvel-Film, Thunderbolts, wieder aufgreifen.
Fernsehserien: Er spielt den grummeligen, aber liebenswerten Therapeuten Dr. Paul Rhodes in der Apple TV+-Comedyserie Shrinking, die für eine dritte Staffel verlängert wurde. Er war auch in der Paramount+-Westernserie 1923 an der Seite von Helen Mirren zu sehen.
Öffentliche Auftritte: Ford und seine Frau Calista Flockhart zeigen sich gelegentlich gemeinsam bei Preisverleihungen, wie den Emmys 2025. Im März 2025 musste er einen geplanten Auftritt als Laudator bei der Oscar-Verleihung aufgrund einer Gürtelrose-Infektion absagen. 
Wissenswertes
Umweltschutz: Ford ist seit 1991 stellvertretender Vorsitzender von Conservation International und engagiert sich stark für den Umweltschutz. Nach ihm wurden sogar eine Spinnen- und eine Ameisenart benannt.
Pilot: Er ist ein lizenzierter Pilot für Starrflügelflugzeuge und Hubschrauber und hat bei mehreren Gelegenheiten Rettungsdienste in der Nähe seines Wohnorts in Wyoming unterstützt.
Privatleben: Ford ist in dritter Ehe mit Schauspielerin Calista Flockhart verheiratet und hat fünf Kinder.

DIE SCHOCKIERENDE WAHRHEIT HINTER DER MASKE: 20 GEHEIMNISSE ÜBER ZORRO (1957), DIE DIR JAHRELANG VERSCHWIEGEN WURDEN!

Jeder erinnert sich an das legendäre „Z“ – drei schnelle, saubere und plötzliche Klingenstiebe. Eine Wand, eine Tür oder eine Weste trugen das Zeichen des maskierten Rächers, das 1957 im Fernsehen zu einer regelrechten Obsession wurde. Es war eine Art stiller Eid, eine Botschaft an die Tyrannen und ein Versprechen an die Gedemütigten. Doch hinter diesem Symbol verbirgt sich ein Paradoxon, das die Geschichte so faszinierend macht: Diese Serie, die von Gerechtigkeit, Ehre und Loyalität handelte, wäre beinahe aufgrund eines sehr realen „Kalten Krieges“ verschwunden. Es war kein Krieg mit Schwertern, sondern ein Krieg der Anwälte, Verträge und Ausstrahlungsrechte. Während das Publikum glaubte, einem unbesiegbaren Helden zu folgen, hätte hinter den Kulissen jede Woche alles zusammenbrechen können. Heute öffnen wir die verbotene Tür zu den Hintergründen von Zorro aus dem Jahr 1957. Ich verspreche dir eines: Am Ende wirst du die schwarze Maske mit völlig anderen Augen sehen. Wenn du mit dieser Titelmelodie aufgewachsen bist, die dir eine Gänsehaut bescherte, oder wenn du die Disney-Serie gerade erst entdeckst, bleib dran. Denn hinter dem Glanz verbergen sich Verletzungen, Zufälle, Geheimnisse und Szenen, die so absurd sind, dass sie wie Legenden wirken. Wir werden die Details sortieren und erzählen, als wären wir selbst dabei gewesen.

Zorro wurde nicht erst 1957 geboren, aber das Jahr 1957 machte ihn unsterblich. Bevor er ein Fernsehheld wurde, existierte Zorro bereits lange in Abenteuergeschichten und Groschenromanen – in einer Vorstellungswelt, in der Kalifornien wie ein Schauplatz aus Staub, Stiefeln und Ungerechtigkeit aussah. Er hatte bereits viele Gesichter und Verkörperungen im Kino, doch 1957 änderte sich alles. Das Fernsehen hielt Einzug in die Wohnzimmer und Disney erkannte eine entscheidende Sache: Wenn man möchte, dass Familien jede Woche wieder einschalten, braucht man einen festen Termin, nicht nur eine isolierte Episode. Es brauchte ein Versprechen, eine fortlaufende Geschichte. Die Serie von 1957 begnügte sich nicht mit kleinen Abenteuern; sie arbeitete mit großen Erzählbögen über mehrere Episoden hinweg, mit wiederkehrenden Feinden und Fallen. Man sah nicht nur eine Folge, man verfolgte ein Schicksal. Ohne es zu wissen, lernten Millionen von Zuschauern eine Lektion, die zur Basis moderner Superhelden wurde: Die geheime Identität ist nicht nur ein technisches Hilfsmittel, sie ist ein Gefängnis und manchmal auch ein Zufluchtsort.

التعويض عن حوادث السير وحوادث الشغل في إسبانيا: مبدأ الحماية الشاملة للضحية
في إسبانيا، يستفيد القاصر إلى حدود 14 سنة من التعويض الكامل عن الأضرار الجسدية الناتجة عن حوادث السير، حتى ولو كان الخطأ راجعًا إلى القاصر نفسه.
ويشمل ذلك، على سبيل المثال لا الحصر:
قطع الطريق أثناء الضوء الأحمر،
العبور من غير الأماكن المخصصة للراجلين،
أي سلوك مخالف لقواعد السير صادر عن القاصر.
في جميع هذه الحالات، تظل مسؤولية سائق المركبة قائمة، ولا يُحتج بخطأ القاصر لنفي أو تقليص التعويض المستحق له، وذلك طبقًا لمقتضيات القانون 35/2015 بتاريخ 22 شتنبر المتعلق بنظام تقييم وتعويض الأضرار الناتجة عن حوادث السير.
كما يجدر التذكير بأنه في حالة وفاة شخص بإسبانيا نتيجة حادثة سير أو حادثة شغل، فإن الضحية أو ذوي حقوقه يستفيدون من نفس التعويض المقرر للمواطن الإسباني، حتى وإن كان الضحية في وضعية إدارية غير قانونية.
وعليه، فإن الوضعية القانونية للمهاجر لا يكون لها أي أثر على الحق في التعويض متى ثبتت صفة الضحية والعلاقة السببية بين الحادث والضرر.
هذا المبدأ يكرّس البعد الإنساني والاجتماعي للتشريع الإسباني، ويؤكد أن التعويض حق مرتبط بالضرر وليس بالوضعية الإدارية.

What does true courage look like — stripped of noise, nationalism, and cinematic chest-thumping?
Too Young To Die reflects on the lives of two Param Vir Chakra awardees, Second Lieutenant Arun Khetarpal and Captain Manoj Kumar Pandey — officers from different generations, backgrounds, and personalities, yet united by a shared moral clarity in moments of impossible choice. Through the lens of Ikkis, a film on Arun Khetarpal’s life, this piece explores leadership not as bravado, but as responsibility, restraint, and the willingness to choose the harder right.
The essay moves between battlefield courage and moral courage — between tanks disabled under fire and quieter moments of accountability, self-doubt, discipline, and duty. It refuses to romanticise war, instead offering a deeply human portrait of soldiers who were barely out of their teens, yet carried extraordinary ethical weight.
At a time when jingoism often passes for patriotism, this is a reminder that the warrior’s code has no room for hatred — and that valour does not need spectacle to endure.

Juba, South Sudan – President Salva Kiir has overhauled the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (TNLA), dismissing 11 members aligned with opposition leader Dr. Riek Machar’s SPLM-IO faction. The move, announced recently, replaces figures like Joseph Malwal Dong, Kuong Dak Wie, and Sandra Bona Malwal with new appointees, including Elizabeth Kanyang Andrew, Nuer Diang, and Buom Tai Gatluak.

The SPLM-IO swiftly condemned the decision as a unilateral breach of the 2018 Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS). Party officials argue it erodes trust between peace partners and jeopardizes the fragile transitional process toward democratic elections.

Critics view these changes as President Kiir’s strategy to bolster his grip on power ahead of the December 2026 polls. The opposition warns that sidelining SPLM-IO voices could tilt the electoral landscape, raising fears of manipulation and renewed instability in the world’s youngest nation.

TNLA spokesperson or relevant official, if available defended the reshuffle as necessary for effective governance, though details on the full list of appointees remain pending. As South Sudan navigates its post-conflict path, this development tests the durability of the peace deal amid mounting political tensions.

To Our Destitute Youth Nuer and Dinka: Let Us Choose Our Own Direction
Our youth are not poor because they lack strength, intelligence, or courage. We are destitute because our energy has been repeatedly hijacked by canny politicians who trade tribal emotions for personal power. They divide us with words, then rule us with our divisions.
For decades, young Nuer and Dinka have been mobilized not to build schools, farms, hospitals, or industries but to defend political interests that do not defend us. We are taught to hate each other while a few grow rich from our anger. This cycle has robbed us of time, education, and opportunity.
It is time to choose a different path.
Our future will not be delivered by politicians who appear only during crises and elections. It will be built by youth who think independently, work together, and refuse to be used as tools of division. Tribal identity is a heritage, not a weapon. When it is used to turn brother against brother, it becomes a chain holding us back.
We must ask hard questions:
Who benefits when Nuer and Dinka fight?
Who loses when schools close and farms are abandoned?
Why are the same leaders always safe while our youth die?
The answers are clear.
True leadership empowers people to think, create, and collaborate. It does not recruit despair. Our direction should be education over mobilization, productivity over propaganda, unity over manipulation. Let us invest our strength in skills, entrepreneurship, agriculture, health, and technology areas that create dignity and lasting peace.
Nuer and Dinka youth share the same struggles: unemployment, poor services, and a stolen future. We also share the same solution refusing to be divided and choosing progress together.
Let us follow our own direction. Not the path of canny politicians, but the road of conscience, cooperation, and country-building.

एक पाकिस्तानी सैनिक अफसर को सकारात्मक रोल में दिखाना भारी न पड़ जाए, इसलिए 'इक्कीस' के निर्माताओं को डिस्क्लेमर जोड़ना पड़ा. इसमें लिखा गया- है- 'पाकिस्तानी ब्रिगेडियर निसार का मानवीय व्यवहार एक अपवाद स्वरूप घटना ही है. अन्यथा हमारा पड़ोसी मुल्क बिल्कुल भी विश्वसनीय नहीं है. पाकिस्तान की सेनाओं ने युद्धकाल और शांति दोनों ही समय में हमारे सैनिकों और नागरिकों के साथ बहुत ही क्रूर और अमानवीय व्यवहार किया है. उनको यातना देने में कई बार जिनेवा कन्वेंशन का खुलकर उल्लंघन किया है. पाकिस्तान द्वारा प्रायोजित आतंकवादी गतिविधियों को देखते हुए एक जागरूक नागरिक के रूप में हमें हमेशा सतर्क और तैयार रहने की जरूरत है. जय हिन्द'...(डिस्क्लेमर कमेंट में देखिए)

श्रीराम राघवन की फिल्म 'इक्कीस' भले ही बॉक्स ऑफिस पर बड़ी सफल न हुई हो, लेकिन युद्ध और सैनिकों के मार्मिक चित्रण के लिए इसकी क्रिटिक्स में सराहना हुई. सोशल मीडिया पर फिल्म की आलोचना भी हुई है, कई यूज़र्स का कहना है कि यह पाकिस्तानी सैनिकों का महिमामंडन करती है...

इस बारे में सीनियर एक्ट्रेस सुहासिनी मुले का बयान गौर करने लायक है.'इक्कीस' में सुहासिनी मुले ने लीड करेक्टर अरुण खेत्रपाल (अगस्त्य नंदा) की मां माहेश्वरी खेत्रपाल का रोल निभाया है...

रविवार को गुवाहाटी प्रेस क्लब में पत्रकारों से बातचीत के दौरान, सुहासिनी मुले ने फिल्म 'इक्कीस' की प्रशंसा करते हुए कहा कि इसमें पाकिस्तानियों को "भूत-प्रेत" या शैतान के रूप में नहीं दिखाया गया है, बल्कि उन्हें "इंसान" के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया गया है...

विभाजन से पहले मदन लाल खेत्रपाल सीमा पार से आए थे और भारत में वो सैनिक अफसर बने. वो विभाजन से पहले लाहौर गवर्नमेंट कॉलेज के छात्र थे. फिल्म में दिखाया गया कि वो लाहौर गवर्नमेंट कॉलेज के पुरातन छात्र रीयूनियन में भाग लेने के लिए बरसों बाद पाकिस्तान गए. वहां उनकी मुलाकात पाकिस्तान के रिटायर्ड ब्रिगेडियर जान मोहम्मद निसार (जयदीप अहलावत) से होती है...वो ब्रिगेडियर मदन लाल खेत्रपाल से अनुरोध करते हैं कि वे जितने दिन पाकिस्तान में रह रहे हैं, उतने दिनों के लिए उनके घर पर ठहरें...

फिल्म में दिखाया गया कि एक दिन धर्मेंद्र के साथ टहलते जयदीप का किरदार कबूल करता है कि उनके टैंक से दागे गए गोले के कारण ही उनके बेटे की मौत हुई थी...

SCHOCK IM PALAST: Prinz William verbannt Camilla – Die eiskalte Rache des künftigen Königs?

Königin Camilla ist wütend. Es ist nicht nur die kleine, höfliche Verärgerung, die man empfindet, wenn ein Protokoll auf einer Tafel geändert wird. Nein, es ist ein kalter, fast persönlicher Zorn. Denn dieses Mal ist es kein Journalist, keine alte Erinnerung oder ein Geist aus der Vergangenheit, der sie verfolgt. Dieses Mal ist es William – der künftige König, der Sohn von Diana. Er, der von Kindheit an gelernt hat zu lächeln, selbst wenn im Inneren alles brennt. Er, der in der Öffentlichkeit niemals die Stimme erhebt, dessen Entscheidungen jedoch wie eine zuschlagende Tür hallen. Das Gerücht, das immer lauter wird, ist simpel, brutal und fast demütigend: William soll gefordert haben, Distanz zu wahren. Keine Nähe mehr, kein Einfluss mehr, keine ständige Präsenz. Als ob Camilla, die nun Königin ist, plötzlich wieder zu einem bloßen Gast herabgestuft werden sollte.

Stellen Sie sich diesen Schock vor. Jahrelang hielt Camilla stand. Sie ertrug die Blicke, die Kritiken, die Beleidigungen und die unmöglichen Vergleiche. Sie wartete geduldig auf ihre Zeit und akzeptierte es, die „böse Figur“ im Roman einer anderen Person zu sein. Doch gerade als die Krone endlich greifbar ist, beginnt die reale Macht – jene, die für die Zukunft zählt – in Richtung William zu gleiten. Und William hat nicht vergessen. Was könnte diesen Wendepunkt ausgelöst haben? War es eine einfache administrative Entscheidung oder der Beginn eines viel tieferen Bruchs zwischen der Vergangenheit und der Zukunft der Monarchie? Es geht hier um alte Wunden, unmögliche Loyalitäten, ein vergiftetes Erbe und eine Wahl, die William als überlebenswichtig betrachten könnte: seine Familie um jeden Preis zu schützen, selbst wenn das bedeutet, die Königin zu kränken. Vielleicht ist es gar nicht Camilla, die er wegstößt, sondern die gesamte schmerzhafte Vergangenheit.

Me Against My Brother: Tribalism in South Sudan

South Sudan, the world’s youngest nation, has a complex history deeply entwined with tribal identities and loyalties. The struggle for power and resources often pits one ethnic group against another, leading to a cycle of violence and mistrust that is difficult to break. At the heart of this issue lies the concept of tribalism, a phenomenon that continues to shape the political landscape and social fabric of the country.

Tribalism in South Sudan is more than just a social construct; it is intertwined with the history of conflict and the quest for independence. Historically, tribes are not only social units; they represent a deep sense of belonging and identity for many South Sudanese. From the Dinka and Nuer to the Shilluk and Equatorians, the divisions among these groups often govern personal relationships and political alliances.

The civil war that erupted in December 2013 was a tragic manifestation of these tribal divisions. What began as a political dispute between President Salva Kiir, a Dinka, and his former deputy Riek Machar, a Nuer, quickly escalated into widespread violence, with both sides drawing on tribal loyalties to further their agenda. The consequences were devastating. Not only did it lead to a humanitarian crisis, but it also deepened existing divides within communities. Families found themselves torn apart, and friendships were strained as allegiances shifted based on ethnicity rather than shared humanity.

The phrase "Me Against My Brother" encapsulates the essence of this tribal conflict. It speaks volumes about the painful reality that many South Sudanese face daily. Traditional values of kinship and solidarity have been warped by the pressures of political conflict and struggle for power, resulting in an environment where trust becomes a rare commodity. Neighbor may turn against neighbor, not out of personal animosity but due to coerced allegiance to one’s ethnic group.

Despite this grim picture, there remains hope for a more peaceful coexistence among South Sudan's diverse population. Emerging voices advocating for national unity rather than tribal loyalty are gaining traction. These individuals, often younger South Sudanese disillusioned by the exclusionary politics of tribalism, are calling for a shared identity that transcends ethnic boundaries. They envision a future where social cohesion is built on mutual respect and understanding, challenging the status quo that has long dictated interactions between tribes.

Education and dialogue are critical tools in addressing the issue of tribalism. By fostering an environment where young people are encouraged to celebrate their own heritage while also respecting others, South Sudan has the potential to cultivate a new generation that prioritizes national unity over tribal affiliation. Community initiatives focused on reconciliation and healing are also essential. Such programs can provide a platform for individuals from different backgrounds to share their stories, breaking down the barriers of misunderstanding that have fuelled conflict.

Ultimately, the journey towards healing and unity in South Sudan is fraught with challenges. However, it is not insurmountable. By confronting the scars of the past and embracing a collective vision for the future, the South Sudanese people can transform "Me Against My Brother" into "We Are One Nation.” Only through concerted effort and commitment to overcoming tribalism can South Sudan truly move towards peace and prosperity for all its citizens.

THEY LAUGHED AS THE ICE WATER HIT HIS MATTED FUR, BUT THEIR SMIRKS VANISHED WHEN THE ALLEY FILLED WITH THE ROAR OF FIFTY HARLEYS AND A LEADER WHO DIDN'T NEED TO RAISE HIS VOICE TO TEACH THEM FEAR.

I still remember the sound of that water hitting the pavement. It wasn’t a splash—it was a slap. A sharp, cruel sound that cut through the dead silence of a November afternoon behind the strip mall. I was sitting in my car, eating a cold sandwich on my break, trying to ignore the gray sludge of the city, when I saw them. Three of them. They couldn't have been older than seventeen, dressed in that effortless, expensive way that screams suburban boredom—varsity jackets, clean sneakers, hair styled just right. And in the corner, wedged between a rusted dumpster and a brick wall, was the dog.

He was a mess of matted brown fur and visible ribs, shaking so hard it looked like he was vibrating. He wasn't growling. He wasn't baring his teeth. He was just trying to disappear into the bricks. They had a cooler—one of those big red ones you take to tailgates. I watched, coffee frozen halfway to my mouth, as the tallest boy tipped it. The water wasn't just cold; it was filled with half-melted ice chunks. He dumped it right over the dog’s head.

The sound the animal made wasn't a bark. It was a high-pitched yelp that sounded terrifyingly human. The boys erupted into laughter. One of them, a blonde kid with a phone in his hand, was circling, getting the angles. "Do it again," he said, his voice muffled by the glass of my windshield but clear enough to make my stomach turn. "I missed the impact."

I wanted to get out. I wanted to scream at them. But I hesitated. I’m not a big guy. I’m forty-five, tired, and I’ve learned the hard way that intervening with groups of teenagers these days can get you hurt or sued. That hesitation is something I still hate myself for. I sat there, hand on the door handle, paralyzed by a pathetic mix of fear and apathy, watching as they refilled the bucket from a spigot on the wall.

"Look at him shake," the tall one laughed, kicking a spray of dirty snow at the dog. "He’s freezing!"

That was when the ground started to hum. 

At first, I thought it was a truck passing on the main road. But the vibration grew, a deep, rhythmic thrumming that rattled the coins in my cup holder. The boys stopped laughing. They looked around, confused. The blonde kid lowered his phone. The sound escalated rapidly from a hum to a roar—a thunderous, synchronized mechanical growl that bounced off the alley walls and amplified until it felt like the air itself was shaking.

Then they turned the corner.

It wasn't just a few bikes. It was a procession. A fleet of heavy touring bikes and choppers, chrome gleaming even under the overcast sky. They rolled into the alley, two by two, blocking the exit completely. The noise was deafening. They cut their engines almost simultaneously, and the sudden silence was heavier than the noise had been. 

There were at least twenty of them. Leather vests, patches that I knew enough not to stare at, heavy boots, and helmets resting on handlebars. They didn't look like weekend warriors; these men looked like they were carved out of granite and bad decisions. 

The teenagers looked small now. The arrogance that had filled the alley ten seconds ago evaporated, replaced by the primal, wide-eyed look of prey realizing the fence is locked. The blonde kid quietly slid his phone into his pocket.

The leader kicked his kickstand down. He was a mountain of a man, beard gray and braided, arms as thick as the boys' legs. He didn't shout. He didn't run. He just swung his leg over the bike and walked slowly toward the dumpster. His boots crunched on the wet gravel. He didn't even look at the boys as he passed them. He went straight to the dog.

The dog cowered, expecting another blow. The big man knelt down—surprisingly graceful for his size—and slowly extended a hand. He let the dog sniff his knuckles. Then, he unzipped his leather vest. Underneath, he was wearing a thick flannel shirt. He took the vest off, the heavy leather creaking, and draped it gently over the soaking wet, shivering animal. 

Only then did he stand up and turn to the boys.

He didn't scream. He didn't curse. He just stared. It was a stare that stripped away their varsity jackets and their parents' money and left them naked in the cold. He took a step forward, and the three boys collectively took a step back, hitting the brick wall.

"Which one of you," the man said, his voice low and scraping like a shovel on concrete, "thinks hypothermia is content?"

Silence. The tall boy, the one with the bucket, was trembling now, his hands shaking worse than the dog's.

"I asked a question," the biker said. He didn't move aggressively. He just stood there, an absolute wall of consequence.

"It... it was just a joke," the tall boy stammered. "We were just... playing."

"Playing," the biker repeated. He looked at the bucket. Then he looked at the ice scattered on the ground. "You like ice? You like being wet in thirty-degree weather?"

The boy shook his head rapidly. "No. No, sir."

"Sir," the biker chuckled darkly. The other men behind him hadn't moved. They were just watching, arms crossed, a silent jury of leather and denim. "I'm not a 'sir,' son. I'm the guy who's going to wait here while you fix this."

He pointed a gloved finger at the blonde kid. "Phone. Now."

The kid fumbled, nearly dropping it before handing it over. The biker looked at the screen, saw the video paused on the screen, and without breaking eye contact, he dropped the phone onto the pavement. He didn't smash it with his foot. He just let gravity do the work, and the screen shattered with a satisfying crunch.

"Oops," the biker said flatly. "Clumsy hands."

He stepped closer, invading their personal space until he was looming over them. "Now. Here is how this game ends. One of you is going into that store to buy dry towels. The best ones they have. Another one is going to buy food. The expensive kind. And you," he looked at the tall boy, "you're going to sit right there on that wet ground next to him until he stops shaking. And if you move before I tell you to, my friends here might get the wrong idea about your hospitality."

I watched from my car, breath held. The tall boy didn't argue. He slowly slid down the wall, sitting in the slush, the cold instantly soaking through his jeans. He looked terrified. 

"Closer," the biker commanded. "He needs body heat."

The boy scooted until his shoulder touched the leather vest covering the dog. The biker nodded, crossed his massive arms, and leaned against the dumpster. "We got all day," he said to the air. "Start warming him up."
